data.title: Freckles (ephelides) — viva
data.summary: Pigmentary disorders · 5 viva questions with answers
data.body:
_Viva questions for the case: **Freckles (ephelides)** (Pigmentary disorders)_

**Q1. What are freckles?**
- Small (1–5 mm) light-brown/red-brown macules on sun-exposed skin of fair-skinned (Fitzpatrick I–II) individuals; appear in early childhood (~age 3), darken in summer and fade in winter
- Strongly associated with red hair/ MC1R variants (red hair colour alleles) — markers of UV sensitivity and melanoma risk

**Q2. Histopathology.**
- Increased melanin in basal keratinocytes with normal number of melanocytes (which are larger and more active); no elongation of rete ridges — unlike lentigo

**Q3. Differentiate freckles from lentigines.**
- Freckles: childhood onset, sun-dependent (fade in winter), sun-exposed sites only, lighter colour, normal melanocyte number, no rete elongation
- Lentigines: any age, not sun-dependent, can be on any site including mucosa, darker, increased melanocytes along basal layer, elongated rete ridges

**Q4. Associations.**
- Axillary/inguinal freckling (Crowe's sign — NF1), xeroderma pigmentosum (freckling in first years of life with marked photosensitivity), Peutz–Jeghers (perioral lentigines — not true freckles), LEOPARD/Noonan with multiple lentigines

**Q5. Management.**
- Reassurance — benign; photoprotection (broad-spectrum sunscreen, clothing) — also reduces skin cancer risk; counsel skin self-examination in fair, freckled individuals
- Cosmetic: hydroquinone/azelaic acid, chemical peels, cryotherapy, Q-switched/picosecond lasers, IPL — recurrence with sun exposure

## Quick spotter facts
- Sun-exposed tiny brown macules darkening in summer in fair child — freckles
- Axillary freckling — NF1

_Sources: Previous-year PG question papers (Sahana P Raju, Solved Papers Dermatology); IADVL Textbook of Dermatology 5e (Hypermelanoses). Answers written in our own words; check with your teachers' preferences._
